title: System log
html:
The guard desk had no picture from camera CAM-04 in the Salle des Etats for part of the evening. Find out who switched it off.

The security system logs every action on every workstation, on the museum's central clock.

Exhibit PDU/04system_log.jsonevery action on the museum workstationsDownload

One event from the log:

{
  "event_id": "EVT-0001",
  "date": "2026-11-13",
  "time": "18:01:24",
  "workstation": "WS-06",
  "action": "lookup_booking",
  "target": "BK-4699",
  "result": "success"
}

Curly brackets hold one event: pairs of a key and a value, such as "action": "lookup_booking". The whole file is a list of events, in square brackets. A login has "target": null: no value.

·

prev_card.title: You spotted the crate
prev_card.html:
The covered crate is CR-017. Going by the time on the still, 20:40:08, the person pushing it is Thomas Lefebvre: his badge opened the corridor door three seconds earlier.

The still and the door log have no ID in common, so you matched them on time. That only works if the camera and the badge readers show the same time.

fields.label: Whose workstation is that? Give the employee ID.

hints: Open system_log.json in VS Code and search for CAM-04 (cmd+F, on Windows ctrl+F). More than one event mentions it: read the action of each.
The event with the action disable_camera and the target CAM-04 names the workstation. staff.csv has a column workstation_id.
EVT-0047: WS-02 switched off CAM-04 at 20:41:08. WS-02 is the desk of Julien Moreau, EMP-015.
